poll_config.description: Encrypted CONFIG poll for enable state, charger/circuit/cable maxima, Bluetooth mode and firmware. Read before current controls.

uid.description: Fresh nonzero request ID; do not reuse within a session.

poll_state.description: Encrypted STATE poll for electrical telemetry and dynamic current. Plaintext response is type 0x41 protobuf.

uid.description: Fresh nonzero request ID; do not reuse within a session.

set_bt_always.description: COMMAND 96 mode 3: advertise continuously so a client can reconnect without a site visit. Confirm Config field 20=3.

set_bt_button_only.description: COMMAND 96 mode 1: advertise only after the touch-button window. Confirm Config field 20=1.

set_charger_disabled.description: COMMAND 29 with Value string false. Confirm code 1 and Config isEnabled absent/0. Does not replace emergency electrical isolation.

set_charger_enabled.description: COMMAND 29 with Value string true. Confirm code 1 and Config isEnabled=1.

set_dynamic_charger_current.advanced_reason: Changes the current a vehicle may draw. 0 A pauses; a positive value resumes and can energize the vehicle. Read Config/State first and enforce the lowest installation limit, then verify command code 1 and the fresh dynamic current. This is not an emergency stop or protective interlock.
set_dynamic_charger_current.description: COMMAND 48 temporary current in whole amperes; 0 pauses, >0 resumes. Cleared by reboot and subordinate to every installer/cable/charger bound.

amperes.description: Serializer bound only. Before sending, clamp to min(current Config circuit/charger maxima, State cable rating and owner continuous limit); never raise an installer setting.

identity.notes: Serial is required in State/Config reads. Treat it and all Structure output as owner-private.

methods.notes: Use a current advertisement and verify the Charge Max serial during onboarding; do not generalize to another Easee model.

host_compatibility.basis: ha-easee-ble README: the tested Charge Max lacks descriptors Linux/BlueZ needs for notification subscription.
host_compatibility.notes: A directly attached adapter commonly receives no notifications. Use an active ESPHome Bluetooth proxy, not passive scanning; interval 320 ms and window 30 ms avoid starving the charger. This is a host-path caveat, not evidence that every BlueZ version must fail.

identification.notes: The vendor service is visible after connecting; advertisements carry Bluetooth SIG company ID 3118 (0x0c26). Advertising is intermittent: enable always-on in the vendor app or long-press the touch button.

device.name: Easee Charge Max (local BLE)
device.notes:
Authenticated local BLE telemetry and deliberately bounded controls for a Charge Max. The owner needs the charger serial and the PIN printed on its label or shown in the app, not an Easee account password. Two EC-JPAKE rounds establish a 32-byte session key; later requests are AES-256-GCM frames serialized as ASCII hex. State/config/structure/debug responses are plaintext six-byte-header protobuf frames; COMMAND replies are JSON.
Only one BLE central can connect. Keep the authenticated link open, serialize requests, and disconnect cleanly. Cloud schedules, OCPP, installer/fuse/circuit settings, Wi-Fi provisioning, RFID maintenance, reboot/self-test, factory reset and firmware operations are outside this spec's control surface.

openness.notes: No public vendor wire specification was found. The sans-I/O public client supplies EC-JPAKE, AES-GCM, framing and commands; the companion integration supplies Charge Max compatibility and host cautions.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: This opens discovery/application onboarding. The host may also display its own OS pairing flow.

procedures.basis: Upstream Charge Max integration setup guide; not replayed here.
procedures.name: Touch-button advertising window

steps.action: Long-press the charger's touch button for 5 seconds.
steps.expect: The charger advertises for a few minutes; exact window duration is not specified.

procedures.basis: Upstream Charge Max integration setup guide and Config field 20 mode 3.
procedures.name: Always-on Bluetooth advertisement

steps.action: Enable Bluetooth always-on in the vendor app, or use the bounded set_bt_always command after authentication.
steps.expect: The charger advertises continuously instead of only after a button press.

exclusivity.notes: The charger has one BLE connection slot; an active proxy also has finite slots and must support pairing.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the current central/integration or vendor app. On an insufficient-authentication/not-paired write refusal, call the host's pair operation and retry. For a stale bond (including CoreBluetooth code 14), remove only the charger from the host's Bluetooth devices, open advertising, pair again, then run EC-JPAKE with fresh nonces.

pairing.notes: The working client bonds before encrypted writes because the vendor characteristics demand ATT encryption. EC-JPAKE is a separate application-layer proof using the label PIN; that PIN is not necessarily the OS pairing passkey, and the OS association model is not established. The one-connection limit is independent of both security layers.

unpair.notes: Forget only the stale host/charger bond in the OS Bluetooth list. No charger-side unpair command or bond-erasing reset is established.

safety_advisory.detail: A 40 A protocol bound is only a serializer sanity limit, not the rating of this charger or its circuit. Before every current write, clamp to the lowest applicable installer circuit maximum, charger maximum, cable rating, dynamic limit and owner-confirmed continuous-load limit. Never use BLE to raise an installer limit. Keep the charger's own protective devices and a qualified electrician's installation as the safety layer; telemetry and a third-party client must not be used to guarantee protection against overheating, fire or vehicle damage.
safety_advisory.summary: BLE current controls are subordinate to the installation and are not an electrical safety interlock.

issued_to_client: The host/charger ATT bond created by the OS Bluetooth stack
A fresh 32-byte EC-JPAKE session key for each connection; ephemeral, never stored as a long-term credential
credentials.notes: The owner supplies PIN and serial. Do not log either derived keys or Structure replies, which can contain account/key material. No Wi-Fi passphrase is sent by this spec.
stored_on_device: ATT link-layer bond material and owner PIN/serial, installer/electrical settings and optional Wi-Fi/cloud/OCPP configuration
Local authorization/RFID data (not read or modified by this spec)

factory_reset.description: Do not issue factory reset, reboot, self-test or installer operations to adopt a charger. Normal BLE migration needs only the current owner PIN and an advertising window.
factory_reset.effect: Command 97 exists in the public command table and is described as untested/irreversible upstream. Its exact effect on owner PIN, Wi-Fi, electrical configuration, RFID records and cloud/OCPP binding is not established and no procedure is offered here.

methods.description: Make the charger advertise, connect through a working active BLE path, exchange two EC-JPAKE rounds with the printed PIN, then keep one encrypted session at a time.

pin.notes: The charger PIN printed on its label or shown in the vendor app. Never log it or the derived session key.

serial.notes: The Charge Max serial used as sn in State/Config poll plaintext.

steps.action: Record the Charge Max serial and label/app PIN locally; do not use the Easee account password.
Long-press the charger's touch button for 5 seconds to open an advertising window of a few minutes, or enable Bluetooth always-on in the vendor app.
steps.expect: An advertisement carrying company ID 3118 appears.

steps.action: Use an active BLE connection path. On Linux/BlueZ, prefer an active ESPHome proxy with scanning interval 320 ms/window 30 ms rather than a directly attached adapter.
steps.expect: HELLO, COMMAND, CONFIG and STATE are available; notification replies arrive.

steps.action: Subscribe to COMMAND, CONFIG and STATE responses and request advisory ATT MTU 333 for the handshake.

Bond this adapter with the charger before encrypted writes. If a write is refused for insufficient authentication/not paired, call the host's pair operation and retry; do not continue on an unbonded path.
steps.expect: The adapter has an ATT-encrypted, bonded link. The charger's label PIN is used next for EC-JPAKE, not assumed to be the OS pairing passkey.

steps.action: Write raw EC-JPAKE round one to HELLO, validate the peer round one and write round two, then validate the server round two and derive the 32-byte key.
steps.expect: Both parties prove knowledge of the PIN; wrong PIN yields an unusable/different key rather than an authenticated control session.

steps.action: Poll State and Config with fresh nonzero request IDs and the serial, then enforce read-back electrical limits before any control.
steps.expect: Valid six-byte-header frames decode. Keep the link open and run one request at a time; disconnect cleanly when finished.

timing.handshake_mtu: 333 advisory; round one is up to 330 bytes
timing.request_rule: One at a time on the authenticated connection; poll interval 30 s is the integration default, 5 s and up is supported upstream.

causes: Open the touch-button window or enable always-on, move an active proxy closer, and close the vendor app/other central.
A proxy scanning continuously starves the radio. Use 320 ms interval/30 ms window with active connections.
troubleshooting.symptom: Nothing advertises or setup times out.

causes: The tested charger lacks descriptors Linux needs. Use an active ESPHome Bluetooth proxy rather than a directly attached adapter.
troubleshooting.symptom: BlueZ connects but notifications never arrive.

causes: Check the printed PIN, serial, per-session nonce freshness and request serialization. A transport reply is not acceptance: COMMAND code must be 1 and Config/State must confirm.
troubleshooting.symptom: Handshake completes but writes fail authentication or return refusals.

causes: The adapter is not bonded. Call pair and retry the write; do not use an unbonded fallback.
The charger forgot the old bond. Remove it from the host's Bluetooth devices, open advertising, pair again, then run EC-JPAKE with fresh nonces.
troubleshooting.symptom: A write reports insufficient authentication/not paired, or an old bond no longer works.

setup.notes: BLE onboarding needs no account or Wi-Fi provisioning. Application authentication is separate: the client must obtain the charger serial and owner PIN, open an advertising window, and complete the handshake. Confidence comes from the public Charge Max implementation and captured-byte tests, not a run by this project.

rejoin.notes: For a new BLE central, close the existing central, open advertising, use its existing ATT bond or pair again, then repeat EC-JPAKE with the same label PIN. If the charger has forgotten the old bond, remove only the stale OS Bluetooth record and pair again. Wi-Fi re-provisioning is deliberately not specified.

steps.action: Disconnect the existing central. If pairing is stale, remove the charger from the host's Bluetooth devices, open advertising, bond, and repeat EC-JPAKE with the current label PIN.

testing.notes: Not driven against a charger by this project. Charge Max is the only model the upstream integration says it physically tested; its 107 offline tests use captured bytes from a real charger. Those tests and the vendor app's authentication constants were reviewed, not replayed. Easee Home, Charge/Core, Equalizer, Charge Max Eichrecht and other backplates are not qualified by this spec.

variants.notes: Only model physically tested by the upstream integration; the scope of every protocol fact and control here.

evidence.open_questions: Exact Charge Max firmware/GATT tree and advertising shape; BlueZ versions and proxy behavior; response fragmentation on other proxies; unknown protobuf fields and schema changes; precise current clamp semantics under every installation; other Easee models, factory reset, firmware and OCPP. The OS pairing association model and any unbonded path remain unproven; no unbonded working path is claimed here.

initialization.description: Run protocol_details.authentication.ec_jpake on every connection before any encrypted request. Raw handshake bytes only; no ASCII-hex wrapper.

Command_Reply.description: JSON object on COMMAND. code 1 means accepted; any other/missing value means refusal.

fields.description: Optional refusal text or a string containing nested JSON; do not assume it is always JSON.
fields.name: Comment

parse_rules: Transport/JSON success is not command success. Require code == 1 and then confirm with fresh Config/State.
If code != 1, show Comment when present; otherwise retain resultcode and other fields. res.nws alone is a network status, not a refusal explanation.

Protobuf.description: Minimal schema-less protobuf decoder for response bodies; field names come only from the confirmed maps in protocol_details.telemetry.
parse_rules: Read a varint key; field number = key >> 3 and wire type = key & 7. Reject field 0, truncated/overlong-varint overflow, unsupported wire types 3/4/6/7 and all out-of-bounds reads.
Wire 0: unsigned varint, at most 64 bits. For signed fields such as localRSSI, if value >= 2^63 subtract 2^64.
Wire 1: exactly 8 bytes, IEEE-754 float64 little-endian. Wire 5: exactly 4 bytes, IEEE-754 float32 little-endian. Preserve NaN/Inf as invalid telemetry rather than clamping.

Wire 2: varint byte length then exactly that many bytes. Decode printable UTF-8 as text, otherwise attempt a bounded nested protobuf object; otherwise retain raw hex/bytes. Never mistake arbitrary bytes for text.

Keep repeated/unknown fields numerically and preserve raw data. Protobuf omits defaults: only protocol_details.telemetry.zero_when_absent may be filled with zero. An absent voltage or unknown field is unknown, not 0.

Response_Frame.description: CONFIG/STATE/STRUCTURE/DEBUG plaintext response: six-byte header followed by schema-less protobuf.

fields.description: 01 01 in captured frames; do not reject a future marker merely because it is unknown.
fields.name: header_marker

parse_rules: Buffer until six bytes are available, read big-endian total length, require length >= 6, then wait for exactly that many bytes. Reject a nonzero first byte or extra bytes attached to a frame as a separate candidate.
When notifications coalesce, parse the first declared frame and feed the remainder through the same parser. Unknown message types are preserved numerically and are not errors.
COMMAND replies do not use this envelope: strict-UTF-8/JSON parse them on their own channel and require code 1 for acceptance.

key_derivation.session_key: Take K's affine x coordinate as exactly 32 big-endian bytes and SHA-256 it. The result is the 32-byte AES key. A wrong PIN can complete messages but produces different/unusable keys; never proceed as if authenticated.

ec_jpake.point_encoding: Uncompressed 65 bytes: 04 || x32_be || y32_be. On the wire, prefix one byte length 0x41.

reference_vectors.source: Public mbedTLS EC-JPAKE reference values preserved by easee-ble tests; password is the standard test string, not an owner PIN. Client x1/x2 and server messages suffice to reproduce pms.

round_one.message: Two independent knowledge/key proofs under the sender's role identity. Client sends X1/X2; server sends X3/X4. Each is TLS_point(Xi) plus its Schnorr proof. Total normally 330 bytes (328-330 depending on minimal r).
round_one.validation: Parse both proofs in order, verify points and proofs, and reject trailing bytes. Do not treat a syntactically valid point as proof of the PIN.

round_two.client_write: G = X3 + X4 + X1; xm = (x2*s) mod n; X = xm*G. Send TLS_point(X) and proof(xm, G, X, 'client'), with no ECParameters prefix.
round_two.server_write: G = X1 + X2 + X3; xm = (x4*s) mod n; X = xm*G. Prefix 03 00 17 (named_curve, secp256r1), then TLS_point(X) and proof(xm, G, X, 'server'). Total 168 bytes normally; client round two is 165.
round_two.validation: Client requires the 03 00 17 prefix and rejects another curve. Verify the round-two proof with the corresponding generator and reject trailing bytes.

ec_jpake.scalar_encoding: Minimal unsigned big-endian, no leading zeros except scalar zero encoded as one zero byte; prefix one byte length. Proofs with zero-length r are invalid.

schnorr_proof.generation: For secret x and public X = x*G, choose v randomly; V = v*G. h = SHA256(uint32be(65)||G_bytes || uint32be(65)||V_bytes || uint32be(65)||X_bytes || uint32be(len(identity))||identity) interpreted big-endian mod n. r = (v - x*h) mod n. Send TLS_point(V) || len(r) || r.
schnorr_proof.verification: Recompute h from the claimed G,V,X and peer identity, then require h*X + r*G == V on the curve and exact consumption of the message.

ec_jpake.secret: Interpret the owner's PIN bytes as an unsigned big-endian integer s. Use cryptographically random scalars in [1, n-1]. Reject the point at infinity, malformed lengths and points not on the curve.

excluded.destructive_maintenance: Reboot 1, self-test 16, factory reset 97, MID/display/maintenance operations and every firmware operation are excluded.
excluded.installer: Commands 21/22/24/47/50 and phase mode 38: fallback/dynamic/max circuit/charger limits, fuse and phase installation settings are not exposed.
excluded.persistence: Only command 48 temporary current is offered for power control. Do not replace it with persistent max-current writes.
excluded.provisioning_access: Wi-Fi 7/53, local authorization/RFID 25/26/33/69/98/99/100/101/102 and cable lock 30 are excluded.
excluded.sensitive: STRUCTURE is never polled; DEBUG has no named fields. Do not publish account/key material.

required_before_current_write: Poll Config/State and establish the lowest current allowed by circuit maxima (Config 8-10), charger max (Config 2), cable rating (State 2), existing dynamic limits and the owner's confirmed continuous-load rule.
Send only command 48 with the clamped whole-ampere value in [0,40]. The 40 is a serializer bound, not hardware qualification.
Require COMMAND code 1 and fresh State field 11 / Config as applicable. A refusal or a different readback is not success.

record_layer.algorithm: AES-256-GCM with the 32-byte session key, empty additional-authenticated-data, a fresh cryptographically random 4-byte nonce and a 16-byte tag.
record_layer.json: Compact UTF-8 with no whitespace. Poll = {"uid":N,"sn":"SERIAL"}. Command = {"Id":N,"Arguments":[{"Id":1,"Value":"..."}]}. Argument values are strings, with booleans lowercase true/false.

reference_vector.expected: Decrypts and authenticates to plaintext. Re-encrypting with the frame's first four bytes as nonce reproduces the exact frame.
reference_vector.notes: Public easee-ble captured-algorithm test with dummy serial; the key/nonce are ephemeral test material, not a reusable charger credential.

record_layer.request_encoding: Binary frame = nonce[4] || tag[16] || ciphertext[len(plaintext)]. Encode the entire frame as lowercase ASCII hex and write those ASCII bytes to COMMAND/STATE/CONFIG. GCM encrypts/authenticates the compact JSON plaintext; there is no outer length prefix.
record_layer.validation: Require key length 32 and binary frame length >=20. Split at 4/16, verify tag before using plaintext, and never reuse a nonce under one session key. Responses on protobuf channels are raw plaintext frames, not ASCII-hex ciphertext.

telemetry.absent_rule: Apply zero_when_absent only to those exact names. Missing voltage, cableRating, unknown fields and absent dynamic circuit fields remain unknown.

11.name: wifiSSID
11.notes: Configured SSID, not proof of connection; redact in diagnostics.

7.name: phaseMode
7.notes: Read-only here; changing it and required disable/enable is excluded.

46.name: ledMode
46.notes: 0 off, 16/17 error, 18 idle master, 21/22 smart not charging/charging, 23/24 normal not charging/charging, 25 awaiting authorization, 29 RFID pairing, 36-39 self-test, 46 Bluetooth connected; preserve other codes.

remaining_unknowns: The OS pairing association model and any unbonded path are unproven; the documented working path bonds before encrypted writes, and no unbonded fallback is claimed.
No other Easee model, including Charge Max Eichrecht, Home, Charge/Core, Equalizer or another backplate, is qualified without a separate capture.
Real Charge Max advertisement/GATT properties and full read-only authenticated session; upstream captures are not this project's hardware test.
Direct BlueZ behavior by version and proxy notification fragmentation; active ESPHome proxy is the reported working route.
Unknown protobuf field meanings and future schema changes; absent unknowns must not be zero-filled.
Exact electrical-limit precedence across every installation/firmware; client-side clamping is mandatory and not a protective interlock.
Factory reset effect, installer operations, phase changes, RFID/Wi-Fi provisioning, OCPP, firmware image/entry/recovery and cloud schedules are deliberately unspecced.
The schema cannot execute EC-JPAKE/AES-GCM sessions or schema-less protobuf; protocol_handler and the supplied vectors are required.

characteristics.name: HELLO
characteristics.notes: Raw EC-JPAKE round-one/round-two messages in both directions. Request advisory MTU 333.

characteristics.name: COMMAND
characteristics.notes: Client plaintext is compact JSON, encrypted and hex-encoded as in protocol_details.record_layer. Replies are UTF-8 JSON, not protobuf: code 1 is accepted; any other code is refusal even when transport succeeds. Check fresh State/Config after every accepted write.

characteristics.name: CONFIG
characteristics.notes: Encrypted poll request; plaintext six-byte-header schema-less protobuf response, message type 0x40.

characteristics.name: STATE
characteristics.notes: Encrypted poll request; plaintext six-byte-header schema-less protobuf response, message type 0x41.

characteristics.name: STRUCTURE (sensitive; not polled)
characteristics.notes: Type 0x42. Can carry account and key material. Do not request, publish or log it from a general telemetry client.

characteristics.name: DEBUG (unnamed fields; not polled)
characteristics.notes: Type 0x43. Decode generically if needed; no field meaning is established here.

characteristics.name: TIME (not exposed on tested Charge Max)
characteristics.notes: Present in the public protocol map but absent on the tested model; do not require it.
